output.reason: [ev-18ac53d77b4b] says only that istio-clean-iptables failed to remove kube-virt-related iptables rules, and that this is now fixed. In the proposed condition, istio-clean-iptables is the name of the tool itself, not a container argument. Treating it as a cli-flag that is set would flag the wrong environments, or none of them. The evidence names no flag, value or setting that creates kube-virt rules. Exposure therefore depends on whether such rules exist on nodes when the clean tool runs, and no static input shows that.

correction.statement: The istio-clean-iptables tool now removes kube-virt-related iptables rules that it previously left in place. Environments are exposed only where kube-virt-related rules were installed and the clean tool runs; the release notes name no configuration that shows this.

exposure.needed: whether kube-virt-related iptables rules are installed on the environment's nodes when istio-clean-iptables runs; the release notes name no configuration setting that produces them
